raw_response:
I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I won’t make big changes this year. My family has only 3 people and some work off-farm, so labor is tight. Cotton can bring cash, but it takes more hand work, especially picking, so I won’t put too much area into it. I’ll keep `4 mu` in cotton and `5 mu` in spring maize in `2026`. Maize is steadier and easier to manage, so I give it a bit more land. Since I have a well, I will irrigate when the crop is at an important stage, but I won’t water too many times because pumping costs money. For fertilizer, I still follow the way that works here: base fertilizer first, then one topdressing when the crop is growing strongly. I’d rather not cut fertilizer too much, because if the crop turns weak later, the yield loss hurts more than saving a little cash now.

For cotton, I will plant in late April, use a local improved variety, give moderate fertilizer, and watch insects closely after squaring. For spring maize, I will plant around late April to early May, use hybrid seed, do one base application and one topdress at jointing, and use herbicide early so weeds don’t steal moisture. I’m aiming for a steady year, not the highest possible yield, because cash and labor both have to be watched.
